Designing, refining, and maintaining agent skills at Perplexity

Agent skills are reusable packages of instructions, examples, and resources that help agents perform specialized work consistently. At Perplexity, we treat them as maintained product surfaces rather than one-off prompt fragments, with clear owners and measurable outcomes for the people who depend on them.

Design around real tasks

A useful skill begins with representative user tasks and the constraints of the runtime. The author identifies the decision points that require judgment, keeps deterministic work in tools, and makes the expected output easy to verify. This keeps instructions focused while preserving the context an agent needs to make sound decisions.

Refinement comes from reviewing failed runs, distinguishing missing context from weak procedure, and updating the smallest part of the skill that explains the failure. Each revision is tested against both the original case and neighboring cases so a local fix does not create a broader regression.

Maintain quality over time

Maintenance includes checking external dependencies, removing stale guidance, and recording why important constraints exist. Teams review changes as product changes: users should experience more reliable outcomes without needing to understand the implementation details behind the skill.

  • Ground instructions in observed tasks.
  • Keep examples representative and testable.
  • Review failures and revise with evidence.
